col-span-full! prose-dropcap"><p>PlanetScale manages cloud database workloads for its customers&#x27; most sensitive data. Reliability is the product and every code change pushed to production must be flawless. As agents made code generation cheap and fast, code review became the new bottleneck in the software development lifecycle.</p>
<p>To ensure correctness and ship code to production with confidence, PlanetScale adopted <a href="https://cursor.com/bugbot" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Bugbot</a> as a dedicated agentic review layer. Today, roughly 80% of Bugbot comments are addressed before merge time, preventing issues from reaching production and saving PlanetScale the equivalent of two full-time engineers worth of review effort.</p>
<h2 id="agents-shift-bottlenecks-in-the-sdlc-downstream" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#agents-shift-bottlenecks-in-the-sdlc-downstream" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Agents shift bottlenecks in the SDLC downstream</h2>
<p>To maintain product reliability, the PlanetScale engineering team sets an uncompromising bar for code review. &quot;Reliability is at the core of our product. Every change pushed to production must be flawless,&quot; said Fatih Arslan, a software engineer at PlanetScale.</p>
<p>As coding agents became central to development workflows, bottlenecks shifted downstream, from code generation to code review. &quot;Code has become cheap. The bottleneck is now whether your code is correct and whether you understand what it does,&quot; explained Arslan.</p>
<p>Code output increased rapidly while human review capacity remained fixed. This imbalance created pressure on product quality. To keep pace, PlanetScale estimated it would need to dedicate two engineers exclusively to code review. That tradeoff would reduce engineering bandwidth for product development without solving the long-term reliability challenge as agent adoption continued to scale.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">We realized we need Bugbot&#x27;s agentic review to complement our existing process. It would otherwise be very difficult to push code to production with confidence in quality and correctness.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Fatih Arslan</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Software engineer, PlanetScale</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="eliminating-production-downtime-with-bugbot" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#eliminating-production-downtime-with-bugbot" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Eliminating production downtime with Bugbot</h2>
<p>Bugbot stood out from other agent review tools in detecting issues that human reviewers were missing because of the complexity of PlanetScale&#x27;s codebase and volume of agent-generated code.</p>
<p>With Bugbot, engineers began catching and resolving bugs that could cause production downtime earlier in development.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">Bugbot is different from other tools. It detects issues that as a human reviewer I would never imagine to look at. I was blown away.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Fatih Arslan</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Software engineer, PlanetScale</div></div></div></div>
<p>Unlike static analyzers and linters that focus on mechanical correctness, Bugbot surfaces deeper semantic and logical issues like:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>State synchronization gaps</strong> where systems are marked complete prematurely</li>
<li><strong>Logical flow changes</strong> that prevent critical code paths from executing</li>
<li><strong>Asynchronous controller interactions</strong> that fail to converge properly</li>
<li><strong>Edge cases</strong> that could trigger restarts across production databases</li>
</ul>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">Bugbot consistently finds bugs that can cause meaningful downtime in production, but are very hard for humans to catch.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Fatih Arslan</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Software engineer, PlanetScale</div></div></div></div>
<p>PlanetScale also found that simply prompting a frontier model to review code would not consistently surface the most critical issues Bugbot identifies. &quot;When I use a reasoning model and ask it to review the branch, it doesn&#x27;t find these issues. It&#x27;s the specialized harness and the way Bugbot is built that makes all the difference,&quot; said Arslan.</p>
<h2 id="measuring-the-quality-of-bugbot-reviews" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#measuring-the-quality-of-bugbot-reviews" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Measuring the quality of Bugbot reviews</h2>
<p>PlanetScale evaluates Bugbot using a simple metric: resolution rate, which measures the proportion of Bugbot-identified issues that are addressed at merge time.</p>
<p>Roughly 80% of Bugbot comments are now addressed by engineers across more than 2,000 PRs reviewed each month. &quot;Bugbot&#x27;s comments are top notch and keep improving over time as Bugbot gets more context,&quot; said Arslan.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">The signal-to-noise ratio for Bugbot is very high. When Bugbot comments on a PR, we know it is highlighting an issue we have to fix.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Fatih Arslan</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Software engineer, PlanetScale</div></div></div></div>
<p>Bugbot is now deeply embedded in PlanetScale&#x27;s workflow and gives engineers the confidence that both human-written and agent-generated code can be shipped safely to production. &quot;I love Bugbot. That&#x27;s my motto,&quot; says Arslan.</p>
<p>PlanetScale can now ship software more quickly without sacrificing quality, while engineers can focus on solving complex infrastructure problems rather than manually reviewing every line produced by agents.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">If I took Bugbot away from our engineering team, there would be a mutiny.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Sam Lambert</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">CEO, PlanetScale</div></div></div></div>
<hr/>

text-theme-text">2K+</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec leading-[var(--leading-cozy)]">PRs reviewed monthly</div></div><div class="flex flex-col gap-v2/12"><div class="type-md-lg text-theme-text">2 FTEs</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec leading-[var(--leading-cozy)]">Dev time saved</div></div></div></div></div></div></aside><div class="prose prose--block prose--blog col-span-full! prose-dropcap"><p>PlanetScale manages cloud database workloads for its customers&#x27; most sensitive data. Reliability is the product and every code change pushed to production must be flawless. As agents made code generation cheap and fast, code review became the new bottleneck in the software development lifecycle.</p>
<p>To ensure correctness and ship code to production with confidence, PlanetScale adopted <a href="https://cursor.com/bugbot" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Bugbot</a> as a dedicated agentic review layer. Today, roughly 80% of Bugbot comments are addressed before merge time, preventing issues from reaching production and saving PlanetScale the equivalent of two full-time engineers worth of review effort.</p>
<h2 id="agents-shift-bottlenecks-in-the-sdlc-downstream" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#agents-shift-bottlenecks-in-the-sdlc-downstream" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Agents shift bottlenecks in the SDLC downstream</h2>
<p>To maintain product reliability, the PlanetScale engineering team sets an uncompromising bar for code review. &quot;Reliability is at the core of our product. Every change pushed to production must be flawless,&quot; said Fatih Arslan, a software engineer at PlanetScale.</p>
<p>As coding agents became central to development workflows, bottlenecks shifted downstream, from code generation to code review. &quot;Code has become cheap. The bottleneck is now whether your code is correct and whether you understand what it does,&quot; explained Arslan.</p>
<p>Code output increased rapidly while human review capacity remained fixed. This imbalance created pressure on product quality. To keep pace, PlanetScale estimated it would need to dedicate two engineers exclusively to code review. That tradeoff would reduce engineering bandwidth for product development without solving the long-term reliability challenge as agent adoption continued to scale.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">We realized we need Bugbot&#x27;s agentic review to complement our existing process. It would otherwise be very difficult to push code to production with confidence in quality and correctness.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Fatih Arslan</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Software engineer, PlanetScale</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="eliminating-production-downtime-with-bugbot" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#eliminating-production-downtime-with-bugbot" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Eliminating production downtime with Bugbot</h2>
<p>Bugbot stood out from other agent review tools in detecting issues that human reviewers were missing because of the complexity of PlanetScale&#x27;s codebase and volume of agent-generated code.</p>
<p>With Bugbot, engineers began catching and resolving bugs that could cause production downtime earlier in development.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">Bugbot is different from other tools. It detects issues that as a human reviewer I would never imagine to look at. I was blown away.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Fatih Arslan</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Software engineer, PlanetScale</div></div></div></div>
<p>Unlike static analyzers and linters that focus on mechanical correctness, Bugbot surfaces deeper semantic and logical issues like:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>State synchronization gaps</strong> where systems are marked complete prematurely</li>
<li><strong>Logical flow changes</strong> that prevent critical code paths from executing</li>
<li><strong>Asynchronous controller interactions</strong> that fail to converge properly</li>
<li><strong>Edge cases</strong> that could trigger restarts across production databases</li>
</ul>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">Bugbot consistently finds bugs that can cause meaningful downtime in production, but are very hard for humans to catch.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Fatih Arslan</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Software engineer, PlanetScale</div></div></div></div>
<p>PlanetScale also found that simply prompting a frontier model to review code would not consistently surface the most critical issues Bugbot identifies. &quot;When I use a reasoning model and ask it to review the branch, it doesn&#x27;t find these issues. It&#x27;s the specialized harness and the way Bugbot is built that makes all the difference,&quot; said Arslan.</p>
<h2 id="measuring-the-quality-of-bugbot-reviews" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#measuring-the-quality-of-bugbot-reviews" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Measuring the quality of Bugbot reviews</h2>
<p>PlanetScale evaluates Bugbot using a simple metric: resolution rate, which measures the proportion of Bugbot-identified issues that are addressed at merge time.</p>
<p>Roughly 80% of Bugbot comments are now addressed by engineers across more than 2,000 PRs reviewed each month. &quot;Bugbot&#x27;s comments are top notch and keep improving over time as Bugbot gets more context,&quot; said Arslan.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">The signal-to-noise ratio for Bugbot is very high. When Bugbot comments on a PR, we know it is highlighting an issue we have to fix.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Fatih Arslan</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Software engineer, PlanetScale</div></div></div></div>
<p>Bugbot is now deeply embedded in PlanetScale&#x27;s workflow and gives engineers the confidence that both human-written and agent-generated code can be shipped safely to production. &quot;I love Bugbot. That&#x27;s my motto,&quot; says Arslan.</p>
<p>PlanetScale can now ship software more quickly without sacrificing quality, while engineers can focus on solving complex infrastructure problems rather than manually reviewing every line produced by agents.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">If I took Bugbot away from our engineering team, there would be a mutiny.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Sam Lambert</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">CEO, PlanetScale</div></div></div></div>
<hr/>
<p>If you&#x27;re excited about streamlining code review and enhancing product reliability with agents, please <a href="https://cursor.com/contact-sales?source=customers" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">reach out to our team</a> to get started with a Cursor trial.</p></div><footer class="mt-v2"><p class="type-base"><span class="text-theme-text-sec">Filed under:<!-- --> </span><a The bottleneck is now whether your code is correct and whether you understand what it does,\\\" explained Arslan.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Code output increased rapidly while human review capacity remained fixed.
